title: Inductive Invariant Proofs and State Space Limits in Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache with Doubly Linked List (TypeScript)
topic: Least Recently Used (LRU) Cache with Doubly Linked List

abstract: Least Recently Used (LRU) caches are ubiquitous in systems that require bounded memory footprints. This work presents a formally verified TypeScript implementation that couples a hash map with a doubly linked list to achieve constant-time access, insertion, and deletion. We establish a precise invariant that the list order always reflects recency of use, and we prove that the invariant is preserved under all public operations. The algorithmic complexity is shown to be $O(1)$ per operation, while the static abstract syntax tree (AST) analysis confirms a structural complexity of $O(N)$ auxiliary memory and a balanced search-style insertion cost of $O(\log N)$. The source code is publicly available at \textbf{Source Code}: \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/typescript-design-patterns/tree/main/algorithms/20261016_051602_least_recently_used__lru__cach}.
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints
